title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Bowing And Prostration With The Universe General Result

questions.question: What does the person think about right before saying “Allah is Most Great” and bowing?
questions.answer: He reflects on Allah’s greatness and on how the sleeping living things and the heavenly bodies are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: How are the plants, animals, suns, and stars described in relation to Allah?
questions.answer: They are shown as obedient servants and like soldiers carrying out His command.

questions.question: In this passage, what does bowing show about a believer’s response to Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: It shows respect, humility, and submission before His power.

questions.question: What large event in creation is compared to a great prostration of all beings?
questions.answer: The passing away and death of creatures, generation after generation, is compared to a universal prostration.

questions.question: How are creatures described when their time of service ends?
questions.answer: They are presented like disciplined soldiers being dismissed from duty in an orderly way.

questions.question: What causes creatures to come to life again after that, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s command brings them back, especially as seen in the revival of spring.

questions.question: What lesson does spring teach in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah can raise beings to life again and prepare them once more for service.

questions.question: How is the human being expected to act after thinking about the death and revival of creation?
questions.answer: He should follow that pattern by saying “Allah is Most Great” and going into prostration before Allah.

questions.question: What feelings should a person have while prostrating, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should feel amazement, love, humility, and a lowering of his ego.

questions.question: What does the passage say prostration becomes for a human being?
questions.answer: It becomes a kind of spiritual rising and nearness to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe the night prayer as fitting and beautiful?
questions.answer: Because it matches the great changes in creation and gives a meaningful way to worship Allah at that time.

questions.question: Why are the five daily prayers set at specific times, according to the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Because each time points to major changes, clear signs of Allah’s rule, and blessings spread through creation.

questions.question: Which part of the prayer is being described when the worshipper says “Allah is Most Great” and bends down?
questions.answer: The bowing part of the prayer is being described.

questions.question: What examples from the world help the worshipper think about Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: The sleeping creatures of the earth and the stars and suns in the sky help him reflect on Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: Why are these created things compared to soldiers and servants?
questions.answer: Because they obey Allah’s order and serve within the world He manages.

questions.question: What command of Allah is mentioned to show His power over creation?
questions.answer: His command that brings things into being instantly is mentioned.

questions.question: What happens to creatures every year and every century in the image used by the passage?
questions.answer: They complete their service and then pass away in an orderly way.

questions.question: How does the passage connect death with prostration?
questions.answer: It presents death as a kind of submission before Allah, like a universal falling into prostration.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens in spring after this widespread passing away?
questions.answer: Many beings are brought back to life and made ready again for their duties.

questions.question: Why is spring compared to a trumpet-blast?
questions.answer: Because it is pictured as a powerful awakening that calls life to rise again.

questions.question: What should a person learn from the way creation dies and comes back?
questions.answer: He should learn to submit to Allah with humility and to worship Him with awe and love.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the person makes a kind of Ascension in prostration?
questions.answer: It means prostration becomes a spiritual elevation and closeness to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the value of praying ‘Isha?
questions.answer: It describes it as beautiful, uplifting, enjoyable, wise, and very important.

questions.question: What is one main reason given for prayer times being fixed instead of random?
questions.answer: They are tied to meaningful moments that show Allah’s actions and blessings in the universe.

questions.question: What does the worshipper notice about the world before he bows in this passage?
questions.answer: He notices signs of Allah’s greatness in the resting creatures on earth and in the heavenly bodies above.

questions.question: What does calling creation “lamps” suggest about the suns and stars?
questions.answer: It suggests they serve a purpose in the world and shine by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What is the worshipper’s spoken response to remembering Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: He says “Allah is Most Great.”

questions.question: What second big reflection comes after bowing is mentioned?
questions.answer: The worshipper thinks about the prostration of all creation.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the death of creatures show about their relationship to Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that they remain under His command and leave their duties in an ordered, obedient way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both yearly and century-long changes?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s power covers both short cycles and long stretches of time.

questions.question: How are revived creatures in spring described after they return to life?
questions.answer: They are described as rising and becoming ready again to serve their Lord.

questions.question: What does the phrase about “insignificant man” teach about the human being?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are small by themselves and should be humble before Allah.

questions.question: What two qualities of Allah are especially remembered when the person prostrates?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy and beauty are especially remembered.

questions.question: Which character traits should grow in a believer during prostration?
questions.answer: Wonder, love, humility, and freedom from pride should grow in him.

questions.question: According to the final sentence, what do the five prayer times point to?
questions.answer: They point to huge changes, Allah’s governing activity, and His blessings throughout creation.

questions.question: What picture of the universe is given when the person prepares to bow?
questions.answer: The universe is pictured as a guesthouse filled with beings that serve Allah under His rule.

questions.question: How do sleeping plants and animals still point to Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: Even in their quiet state, they show that they remain under His control and order.

questions.question: Why are the stars called serious or sober in meaning?
questions.answer: It shows them as steady, ordered, and obedient within Allah’s system.

questions.question: What does the worshipper do after reflecting on Allah’s greatness in creation?
questions.answer: He says “Allah is Most Great” and bows.

questions.question: What does the passage compare creatures to when they leave this world?
questions.answer: It compares them to an organized army or obedient soldiers being dismissed.

questions.question: What does this comparison teach about death?
questions.answer: It teaches that death is not chaotic but happens under Allah’s command and wisdom.

questions.question: What example in nature is given to show that life can return after death?
questions.answer: The return of life in spring is given as the example.

questions.question: How should a human being respond to the revival seen in spring?
questions.answer: He should join creation in worship by glorifying Allah and prostrating before Him.

questions.question: What is meant by “dignified self-effacement” in this passage?
questions.answer: It means putting aside pride in a noble way and standing humbly before Allah.

questions.question: Why is prostration more than just a body movement in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it expresses deep faith, humble love, and a spiritual rising toward Allah.

questions.question: What overall judgment does the passage give about the ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It presents it as noble, enjoyable, appropriate, and very serious.

questions.question: Why is it called wise for the required prayers to be linked to certain times?
questions.answer: Because those times match powerful signs of Allah’s actions and the blessings He gives everywhere.

questions.question: What does the worshipper remember about Allah before going into bowing?
questions.answer: He remembers Allah’s majesty and control over all living things and heavenly bodies.

questions.question: How are created things in the world presented as serving Allah?
questions.answer: They are shown as obedient workers and troops carrying out His will.

questions.question: What words does the worshipper say as an expression of glorifying Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: He says “Allah is Most Great.”

questions.question: What universal event does the passage describe as if all creatures are making sujood?
questions.answer: Their death and departure from their tasks are described like a universal sujood.

questions.question: What does the orderly passing of creatures suggest about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: It suggests that His rule is perfect, controlled, and full of wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage use the image of spring to build hope?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah can bring life back after lifelessness and prepare creation again for service.

questions.question: In what way is the human being supposed to follow the rest of creation?
questions.answer: He is supposed to glorify Allah, humble himself, and prostrate before Him.

questions.question: What emotions are joined together in the believer’s prostration?
questions.answer: Awe, love, humility, and surrender are joined together.

questions.question: Why is human smallness mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: To remind people not to be arrogant and to recognize their need to worship Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says prostration is a kind of Ascension?
questions.answer: It means lowering oneself before Allah becomes a way of spiritual elevation.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate the duty of ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It says it is a beautiful, joyful, elevated, and fitting act of worship.

questions.question: What three things does each prayer time point to, according to the last sentence?
questions.answer: It points to a major change, Allah’s powerful management, and widespread divine blessings.

questions.question: What thought leads the worshipper to bow during the night prayer?
questions.answer: Thinking about Allah’s glory and the obedience of creation leads him to bow.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are mentioned to show this obedience?
questions.answer: Sleeping plants and animals, along with the suns and stars, are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the image of soldiers under command teach about creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation is not independent but follows Allah’s authority.

questions.question: After bowing, what larger scene does the worshipper reflect on?
questions.answer: He reflects on all creatures as if they are making a great prostration through their passing away.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the end of creatures’ worldly duties?
questions.answer: It describes them as being released from service in a disciplined and ordered way.

questions.question: What role does Allah’s command play in both death and renewed life in the passage?
questions.answer: By His command, creatures leave their service, and by His command, they are brought back again.

questions.question: What season especially shows the return of life?
questions.answer: Spring especially shows it.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from the actions of creation to the actions of a human being?
questions.answer: To show that people should learn from creation and respond with worship and humility.

questions.question: How is the believer’s sujood described in spiritual terms?
questions.answer: It is described as full of loving amazement, humble surrender, and a kind of rising toward Allah.

questions.question: What does this passage teach about the relationship between humility and honor in worship?
questions.answer: It teaches that lowering oneself before Allah is not shameful; it is an honorable way to draw near to Him.

questions.question: What conclusion is given about performing the ‘Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It is presented as a noble, pleasant, meaningful, and serious duty.

questions.question: Why is it proper for the daily prayers to be assigned to set times?
questions.answer: Because those times mark great changes in the universe and remind people of Allah’s actions and blessings.
